title: Five o'clock — the Mongolia sails
learning_goal: Know that the ship at the end of the leg is a real scheduled mail steamer, hedged where the record is thin; feel Europe closing behind us.

narration.script: Four o'clock, Saturday afternoon. One hour. The quay is still called the stazione marittima — the harbour station, where the train meets the ship. And here is the Mongolia: in the novel, iron, two thousand eight hundred tons, taking on the Indian mail. A real P&O Mongolia did exist, launched in 1865, about three thousand tons. Whether she was on this run that Saturday, nobody has shown us. Five o'clock. She sails.

variants.clear: Four o'clock, Saturday afternoon. One hour to wait. The quay is still called the stazione marittima — the harbour station, where the train meets the ship. And here is the Mongolia. In the novel she is iron, two thousand eight hundred tons, and she takes on the Indian mail here. A real P&O ship called Mongolia did exist: launched in 1865, about three thousand tons. Whether she was on this route that Saturday, nobody has shown us. Five o'clock. She sails.

RUNDOWN CORRECTION APPLIED: the manifest's master spec said 'Brindisi 4 p.m. 4 Oct'; F-50 gives SATURDAY 5 OCTOBER for the arrival and the sailing, and Turin is the 4th. Fix it in the master, not only here.

production_notes: SEGMENT 8, last third (50 s; 71 words — the segment totals 199 against its 205 ceiling). THE CHAPTER ENDS ON DEPARTURE (rundown Decision 1, built as recommended): horn, the ship leaves, the sea leg draws south-east, and Day 3 opens at sea. Reversing it costs one edit — cut at 36 s, drop M-251, end on the column. HEDGING IS THE WHOLE CRAFT OF THIS SCENE: F-59 is med, so the real ship is 'about three thousand tons' and 'a real P&O Mongolia did exist', and the sentence 'Whether she was on this run that Saturday, nobody has shown us' is in BOTH tracks, because the qualifier travels with the claim. NEVER state a master or a passenger list (the fact sheet's own instruction). Verne's '2,800 tons' is quoted as the novel's figure, in a caption, and the guide attributes it aloud with 'in the novel'.
